references.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
references.support: Separates harm magnitude from likelihood, calls for contextual evidence, and states that unmeasurable risk is not automatically high or low.
references.limit: Does not validate atomOS capabilities. The rainbow and musical-note scale is an original analyst rubric, not official NIST scoring.

references.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
references.support: Supports empirical capability evaluation, provenance review and incident monitoring; cautions against extrapolating performance from narrow assessments and covers information, privacy and integration risks.
references.limit: Applies to generative AI contexts, including teacher acquisition; it does not establish that the LUT engine has general language capabilities.

references.title: Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security
references.status: NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3; final technical guidance
references.support: Addresses security where programmable systems interact with physical processes, including safety-system independence, network separation, tested updates and recovery planning.
references.limit: Relevant to actual physical-system integration. It neither certifies this kernel nor establishes that a software formalization directly controls matter.

references.title: Recommendation on the Ethics of Neurotechnology
references.status: UNESCO Recommendation; adopted ethical standard-setting instrument
references.support: Supports informed, voluntary and withdrawable participation; safeguards against coercion and manipulation; protects mental privacy and limits sensitive-data collection and processing.
references.limit: An ethical Recommendation, not itself binding national law or evidence that atomOS can read minds or control mental states.

references.title: Global guidance framework for the responsible use of the life sciences: mitigating biorisks and governing dual-use research
references.support: Supports anticipatory biorisk assessment and shared governance responsibilities across the research lifecycle, including researchers, institutions, funders and other stakeholders.
references.limit: Provides governance principles, not biological procedures or proof that this kernel enables a particular biological capability.

references.title: WebXR Device API
references.support: Identifies XR privacy, security and comfort concerns involving sensitive pose data, user intention, consent, profiling and user control over immersive sessions.
references.limit: A draft technical specification, not a safety certification or evidence that the present kernel implements XR sensing.

references.title: XR Accessibility User Requirements
references.status: W3C Working Group Note; exploratory user requirements
references.support: Discusses accessible escape controls, time awareness, orientation reset, alternative output routes, adjustable interaction speed and avoidance of sickness triggers.
references.limit: Explicitly not baseline conformance requirements; supports design considerations rather than certification, binding law or universal medical safety guarantees.

references.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
references.support: Success Criterion 1.4.1 supports labels and other visual distinctions alongside color, so the atlas remains understandable without identifying its rainbow swatches.
references.limit: Using this principle does not establish PDF accessibility conformance. The musical labels and severity assignments are original analyst choices.
